clue.text: Foolish talk about why it's said I like immature men

indicators.note: about means going round, so the talk wraps itself around what follows

parts.note: bosh is nonsense, empty chatter

indicators.note: something that is said is only heard, so the word before it counts for its spoken sound

parts.note: the letter Y is pronounced like the word why
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses chatter about why they find childish men attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken Y and the I sit together inside BOSH: BO(Y I)SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyish describes behaviour or looks typical of a young lad, which fits grown men who never quite matured.

clue.text: One may speak to house surgeon wanting training

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the surgeon is without some letters

parts.note: a surgeon operates, so is an operator
PE is physical education, school exercise training

explanation.surface: A doctor in a hospital is addressed by someone lacking proper training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House surgeon' looks like a junior doctor, but house is part of the definition, the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is a public speaker, such as one who addresses the chamber in parliament.

clue.text: Drink author's left out of authoritative guide

parts.note: the author speaking of himself says I am, I'M

indicators.note: left out of the guide means removed from it, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: a bible is the definitive reference book on a subject
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A writer is offended at being omitted from a definitive reference work and turns to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the author or setter is I or ME, so author's means I'M; BIBLE without L is BIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink, especially alcohol, a formal or jocular verb for swallowing liquid.

clue.text: Charm of heroin's heightened by weed

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin; heroin's as heroin is
to hoe is to weed the ground

explanation.surface: Drugs talk: the appeal of heroin is boosted by cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' suggests cannabis but is the gardening verb; in a down answer, heightened by HOE means it sits on top of HOE.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe is a traditional good-luck token, often hung above a door as a lucky charm.

clue.text: Acknowledge being given a hand to photograph one area of East London

parts.note: to take a picture is to photograph it
a means one
Bow is a district in the East End of London

explanation.surface: A performer applauded by onlookers poses for a picture somewhere in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given a hand' is applause, not help: TAKE + A + BOW. Bow is the district whose bells define a true Cockney.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers bend forward to thank an audience after receiving applause, the stage gesture of recognising clapping.

clue.text: Regularly strives to get even

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone keeps trying hard in order to settle a score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get even' sounds like revenge, but means finish level in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitors who tie finish with equal scores, drawing level with each other.

clue.text: Cook a lot of baked beans for starters and meat course

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is cut
to cook something is to work it into a new form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the word without its final letter

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A menu instruction: prepare plenty of baked beans as an appetiser, then a meat dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' and 'course' make a meal of the surface; only 'meat course' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A kebab is a dish of grilled meat pieces on a skewer, served as the main part of a meal.

clue.text: One helps serviceman adjust navigational aid on phone

indicators.note: words heard over a telephone are only heard, so the phrase counts for its sound

parts.note: to alter is to adjust; a buoy is a floating marker guiding ships, said BOY in British English

explanation.surface: A helpful person talks a soldier through fixing his GPS by telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serviceman' looks military but means a priest taking a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar boy assists the priest during a church service, carrying things and ringing bells.

clue.text: You'll need some breaks if you want to make it

definitions.text: You'll need some breaks if you want to make it

parts.words: You'll need some breaks if you want to make it
parts.note: surface reading: advice that success requires lucky opportunities
setter's reading: eggs must be cracked to cook this dish, as the proverb says

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says you cannot make one without breaking eggs; 'breaks' pretends to mean lucky chances.
explanation.definitionFit: This folded egg dish needs eggs to be cracked open before it can be cooked in the pan.

clue.text: Large party of press men introduced to social gathering

parts.note: to jam is to press or squeeze

indicators.note: something introduced to a gathering is brought into its midst, so it goes inside

parts.note: a bee is a get-together for work or fun, like a quilting bee
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Journalists turn up at a big social event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press men' looks like reporters, but press is JAM and men is OR: JAM + B(OR)EE.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a lively large-scale celebration, especially a big rally of Scouts.

clue.text: Bug that woman's added to computer program

parts.note: a bot is an automated software program
her is the pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: Someone's code has been altered to include a woman, suggesting a software glitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' in a computing surface wants to be a glitch; here it is the verb meaning annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to pester or annoy them, exactly what bother means as a verb.

clue.text: Jerky movement of King trapped by tree trunk

indicators.note: whatever is trapped by something is held inside it

parts.note: a bole is the trunk of a tree
B.B. King was the American blues guitarist

explanation.surface: A monarch is pinned under a fallen tree and twitches.
explanation.walkthrough: King here is not R or K but the blues musician B.B. King, giving BO(BB)LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobble is a small bouncing or jolting motion, as of a ball bobbling over uneven ground.

clue.text: Bribed two journalists working to overcome resistance on the inside

parts.note: a sub is a subeditor, the first of the pair

indicators.note: to overcome something is to get over and around it, so this word wraps the next
put on the inside means placed within the other pieces

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
R is the physics symbol for resistance
an ed is an editor, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: A tale of corruption: two reporters work together to beat opposition from within an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The two journalists are a subeditor and an editor, standard crossword newsroom staff; they sit either side of the working part, which itself has R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To suborn is to induce someone to commit wrongdoing such as perjury, typically by payment.

clue.text: Fish evolved ears to absorb noise

indicators.note: to absorb is to take inside, so the result holds the next item
something that has evolved has changed form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A sea creature developed hearing organs to take in sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The sardine is a small oily fish of the herring family, often sold in tins.

clue.text: Position was filled separately by present contest

indicators.note: the word is filled at two different points, each gap taking a different filling

parts.note: taken as written
someone present is here
a bout is a boxing or wrestling contest

explanation.surface: Someone's place was taken up in turn by a current competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separately' means WAS is split twice, each gap getting its own filling, rather than one insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's whereabouts are their location, the place where they can be found.

clue.text: Human Resources deducting £1 from debts?

indicators.note: deducting means subtracting, so letters are taken away

parts.note: liabilities are debts owed
L is the pound sign's letter, and I is one

explanation.surface: A personnel department is cutting one pound from what it owes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Human Resources' looks like the personnel office, but means people's talents; take L and I from the front of LIABILITIES.
explanation.definitionFit: People's skills and talents are the resources a human being has, a playful reading of the office name.

clue.text: Behave extravagantly, dressing friend of Dorothy in frock

indicators.note: dressing someone wraps clothing around them, so one item goes round another
in places one item within the other

parts.note: a gown is a frock or dress
Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: Someone goes overboard putting a gay man in a dress, 'friend of Dorothy' being old slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friend of Dorothy' is a coded phrase for a gay man, but here it is literal: her dog in The Wizard of Oz. GO(TOTO)WN.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to town is an idiom for doing something lavishly, without restraint or regard for cost.

clue.text: 2 + 2 using binary composition

parts.note: the answer to clue 2, the public speaker
the number two written in binary is 10, read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A sum written in binary code is called a composition, like a schoolroom puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 2 is a cross-reference to 2 down; the second is the number itself, binary 10.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical composition for orchestra, choir and soloists, often on a sacred theme.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval about desire is, in other words, middle class

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cry goes round the next word

parts.note: boo is the jeer of a disapproving crowd
an urge is a strong desire
taken as written
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: A sneer at aspiration is just snobbery about the middle classes.
explanation.walkthrough: BO(URGE)O + IS + IE: the jeer opens to hold the desire.
explanation.definitionFit: The bourgeoisie is the social stratum of property-owning, conventional people between workers and aristocracy.

clue.text: Improve care for mental cases

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the words hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: A call to improve treatment for psychiatric patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' looks like patients but is a verb: the phrase contains the answer, ca(RE FOR M)ental.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform something is to change it for the better, correcting faults in a system or person.

clue.text: Arrive at total

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to reach a decision or conclusion
second meaning: to add up to a sum

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as reaching a sum, but splits into two meanings of one phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both reaching a decision and amounting to a figure, as a bill does.

clue.text: Where one might get bargain alcohol from high street store

parts.note: Boots is a chain of chemist shops on British high streets
ale is beer, an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A shopper hunts for cheap drink from a well-known chain store.
explanation.walkthrough: A car boot sale is a British market where people sell unwanted goods from the boots, or trunks, of their cars.
explanation.definitionFit: At a car boot sale, private sellers offer second-hand goods cheaply, so shoppers often pick up bargains there.

clue.text: One would benefit from this being equally firm

parts.note: as means to the same degree, as in as tall
something set is firm or solid, like a jelly

explanation.surface: A firm would profit from being run on fair, equal terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company but is the adjective meaning solid.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something valuable or useful, an advantage that brings benefit to its owner.

clue.text: Cooler antelope reportedly seen on east of reserve

parts.note: reserve as cool aloofness is ice in one's manner

indicators.note: reported things are passed on by word of mouth, so the animal counts for its sound

parts.note: a bok is a South African antelope, as in springbok, and the plural sounds like a container

explanation.surface: An antelope is spotted on the eastern side of a game reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' suggests a wildlife park but means coolness of manner; in an across answer east is to the right, so the sound of BOKS follows ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is a refrigerated chest or old-style fridge for keeping food and drink cold.

clue.text: Poet's written about love for stage

indicators.note: written about means wrapped around, so the poets enclose the next item

parts.note: bards are poets; poet's read as poets
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A poet's verse about love is meant for the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' reads as a plural, poets, which become BARDS around O.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread the boards is to act; the planks of a theatre floor stand for the stage itself.

clue.text: Get very cross with one replacing young man's last partner

indicators.note: replacing means taking the place of a letter, so one item swaps in for another
last points to the final letter of the young man as the one swapped out

parts.note: a boy is a young man
a lover is a romantic partner
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is furious to find another taking their place with a young man's latest partner.
explanation.walkthrough: BOY LOVER, with I replacing the last letter of BOY, gives BOIL OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To boil over is an idiom for losing one's temper as rage spills out like liquid from a pan.

clue.text: Have intercourse with teacher?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a ...., Bachelor of Education, the degree held by many teachers

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a teacher is only one who holds the degree, B.Ed.
explanation.definitionFit: To bed someone is slang for sleeping with them; B.Ed. is the teaching degree, standing for its holder.

clue.text: Undo belt incorrectly fastened? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: something done incorrectly is done wrongly, so these letters are out of order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone fumbles with a belt, unsure whether it was done up properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is reversed by 'Quite the opposite': not fastened but its contrary.
explanation.definitionFit: A door unbolted has had its bolt drawn back, so it is open, the reverse of secured.

clue.text: It's representative of instrument's sound

indicators.note: sound here means how the word is heard when spoken, not the noise the instrument makes

parts.note: a cymbal is a brass percussion instrument

explanation.surface: A musical instrument's tone is typical of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like the instrument's noise but signals the spoken form of the word cymbal.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol is a sign or emblem that stands for something else, so it represents it.
